The establishment instruction describes an ascending ramp: start with the lightest available load and add the smallest increment between preparatory sets while at least the target reserve remains with stable technique; the working load is the heaviest such load; load and convention are recorded.

After establishment, a load or repetition step requires a logged set record meeting target repetitions with reserve >= prescribed RIR - 1; otherwise the dose holds. A logged load above the planned load is adopted only when that exposure meets this criterion and only up to one smallest increment above the plan, never above a re-establishment ceiling; otherwise the planned load stays the reference and the logged load is asked about. A logged load at or below the plan is executed evidence; a changed known load is a modification (D44).
RIR is treated as approximate (about one repetition of error); technique and comfort govern continuation and stopping.
Fail-closed: no ESTABLISH rows are emitted when this boundary is not enabled.

A load logged on an establishment row becomes a prescribed numeric (KNOWN) load only after the athlete confirms it, after a second logged exposure within one smallest increment of it, or when it lies within one smallest increment of the athlete's own reported load hint; until then the next exposure is FROM_LOG with no number stated and the logged value is asked about (D45).

limitations: Evidence for RIR accuracy in never-trained adults is thin.

Repeated adverse responses (two comparable within 14 days at the current dose after any regression) regress one step; a single adverse response holds.

Any run, easy included, within sameSessionGapHours before MODERATE/HEAVY lower-body work carries a strength-axis cost when strength has a development role; no tie-break depends on candidate identifier strings; equal-harm opposing trade-offs under a JOINT lead are ASKed.

Quality-run-first may be the default for an equal-standing athlete only when the alternative places MODERATE/HEAVY lower-body work within nextDayGapHours before the key run; the choice is disclosed as a reversible population-based default, the athlete may choose otherwise, and repeated comparable athlete evidence may override it; for accustomed lifters the asymmetry is weaker and must be disclosed as such.

Unknown arrangement-level response is admissible only when current whole-week tolerance covers the same task set and frequency, the candidate's worst H0 severity is <= LOW, and it introduces no same-day pairing absent from the athlete's reported routine; otherwise it needs arrangement evidence or ASK; adverse arrangement evidence excludes it.
The trace names the decisive comparison (for example LOWEST_WORST_CASE_JOINT_HARM) whenever non-identical candidates were compared.
No universal spacing minimum; the gap bins rank options and never forbid a feasible arrangement by themselves.

Cold start: same-day pairings arising from the athlete's own chosen days and shifts are admissible and ranked; when the selected arrangement carries a MODERATE or higher H0 cost the program discloses it and offers the shift or day change as a negotiation option.

Near an event, arrangements follow days to the race: no strength in the last raceWeekStrengthMinDaysBeforeRace days; at most one short light session (raceWeekStrengthSets sets, main lifts, RIR >= raceWeekStrengthMinimumRir) on the strength day furthest from the race inside the race window; strength on taper days takes the taper dose.
limitations: Asymmetry evidence is acute and partly from unaccustomed lifters; chronic consequences of next-day arrangements are inferred.
Gap bins are operational.
Upper-body interaction claim relies on the local nature of interference, not a dedicated trial.

SHORT (<= shortMaxDays): resume the last executed doses; the first quality slot runs easy; the next step waits for executed sessions.

MODERATE (<= moderateMaxDays): run entry from a current demonstration (modality RUN, easy/long/recovery-easy family, completed, conversational effort, compatible response, ordinary and next-day function, observed after the interruption began and within currentDemonstrationMaxAgeDays) or the reviewed 15-minute entry; at most moderateStepsToPrior conditional steps to the prior executed dose, each within the single-run ceiling of R6-PLANNED-PROGRESSION.

EARNED is unavailable during RETURN/RESTART; surplus counts only observations after the return started.

Supported events are 10K and half-marathon only; one taper week plus the race week, progressive: taper-week easy runs within taperWeekRunVolumeRange and the long run within taperWeekLongRunRange of the executed peak; taper quality total work minutes within taperQualityWorkRange; race-week easy runs within raceWeekRunVolumeRange; the policy states these are per-session fractions.

Frequency is maintained; intensity is maintained only through work already executed in build/specific weeks; a race-effort touch at the policy dose >= raceWeekTouchMinDaysBeforeRace days before the race requires R6-RUN-QUALITY and an executed comparable quality session; shakeout strides require executed strides; otherwise easy.

Strength stays at a reduced dose: taper sets about taperStrengthSetFraction of the preceding dose at RIR >= 3; race week one session of raceWeekStrengthSets at RIR >= raceWeekStrengthMinimumRir no later than raceWeekStrengthMinDaysBeforeRace days before the race; no new exercise, load increase or rotation.

Post-event: no running before postEventFirstRunMinDaysAfterRace days; runs optional and easy within postEventEasyMinutes; one light strength session; redevelopment (NEXT_BLOCK) requires an eligibility and function assessment dated after the race; redevelopment fractions are declared in the policy.
The legacy path uses the athlete's event kind and only policy-declared fractions.
No finish-time, readiness or peak-performance claim.

Event proximity counts days to the race (raceWindowDays 6; 7 taper days per taper week before the window): race-window sessions have no long run and no quality, an optional shakeout the day before, at most one race-effort touch on the run day closest to the race that is >= raceWeekTouchMinDaysBeforeRace days out, and short easy runs; taper-day sessions take taper doses whichever calendar week they fall in; post-race sessions follow the post-event rules by days since the race; a race date marked unavailable is asked about.
In WALK_JOG or RESTART mode, taper-day, race-window and post-event run sessions are reductions or holds of the achieved session of that mode, never a continuous run the mode has not reached (D43a).

When the run mode entering the race window is WALK_JOG or RESTART, or EVENT_AMBITIOUS_FOR_CURRENT_RUNNING applies, race day is a completion prescription at conversational effort with walk breaks (jog bouts no longer than achieved), without strides and without an instruction to press; race-day warm-up strides for any athlete only after executed strides (D43b-c).
The event negotiation states that the race is longer than any prepared session and offers keep-with-walk-breaks or a later or shorter event; it may stay non-blocking for the preparatory weeks (D43d).
limitations: Taper evidence is from trained athletes; recreational evidence observational.
Combined run+strength taper evidence is indirect.
Post-event recovery evidence is from a simulated half-marathon.
The 6-day race window and the 7-day taper-day split are operational; completion with walk breaks is supported only indirectly (run/walk trial in marathoners, abstract only).
requiredRuntimeChanges: D43 (R6-EVENT-TRANSITION) r6-program.mjs eventWeekSessions/buildWeek (taper days, race window, post-event days), r6-prescription.mjs racePrescription and policy operational.event: event-rule sessions ignore the run mode. Probe C: a novice at walk/jog ladder step 5 (3-minute jog bouts) gets three continuous 15-minute easy runs in the taper week and two in the race week; the race is prescribed at 'hard but controlled' (10K) or 'steady-hard' (half marathon) effort with 'a few relaxed strides' in the warm-up and 'decide in the final part whether to press' for walk/jog, restart and below-minimum athletes alike, while the plan's own EVENT_AMBITIOUS_FOR_CURRENT_RUNNING item promises completion with walk breaks. Required: (a) in WALK_JOG or RESTART mode, taper-day, race-window and post-event run sessions are reductions or holds of the achieved session of that mode (walk/jog at the achieved or a lower step with fewer repetitions; shorter restart runs), never a continuous run the mode has not reached; (b) when the mode entering the race window is WALK_JOG or RESTART, or EVENT_AMBITIOUS_FOR_CURRENT_RUNNING applies, race day is a completion prescription at conversational effort with walk breaks (jog bouts no longer than achieved), no strides and no instruction to press; the race-effort version is never their default; (c) race-day warm-up strides only after executed strides, for every athlete; (d) the negotiation item states that the race is longer than any prepared session and offers keep-with-walk-breaks or a later or shorter event; (e) declare (a)-(c) in operational.event and add the probe-C cases as regression tests.

conditions: Scope: offline synthetic Node24 reference only, for the adult (18+) recreational nonclinical V1 population stated in PROGRAM_POLICY_R6.population. Missing current eligibility is ASK; pain, injury, illness, functional limitation or a clinical interruption reason is CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED with no substitute dose.

Binding: this record binds canonical policy hash e9c87e09d35496791c6d6894639652a4c7bd6cbf6f0b01299d57dd7352373f87 (value.mjs hash). Any policy byte change invalidates it; any change to the runtime functions named in requiredRuntimeChanges needs a delta binding review before runtime freeze.

Operational values are reversible coaching choices inside the envelope, never physiological thresholds, injury-prevention rules, readiness scores, finish-time promises or individual-response predictions.
Steps advance only on executed comparable work without an adverse signal; nothing progresses from elapsed calendar time alone; completed history and official plan state stay immutable.
Causal time: no future or future-reported facts; day-precision facts receive the latest causal instant of that local day; clock skew beyond futureClockSkewSeconds is excluded.

Duplicates merge; the same event identifier with different facts and disagreeing duplicates are quarantined; stale facts beyond maximumAgeDays leave learning and gating but stay in the completed-work ledger.
Partial executions count only for adherence and hold the step; missing effort or heart rate is unknown, never adverse.

Comparability: identical prescription hash and arrangement pool across FOUNDATION/BUILD/DEVELOPMENT/SPECIFIC/CONSOLIDATION/ESTABLISHMENT labels; TAPER, EVENT/RACE_WEEK, POST_EVENT, REVIEW and RETURN/RESTART-mode observations never pool with build-class observations.
Consolidation-week observations may support HOLD or REGRESS but not EARNED surplus.
Arrangement-preference queries include the phase class and a dose key; outputs are associative ranking among admissible options only, never dose authority, causal or clinical inference.
G03 adherence/comparability semantics remain jointly owned by Product/UX and Data; this record does not close G03.

The completed-work record is append-only: a report conflicting with another for the same session (same event identifier with different facts, different physical facts or responses, or one wearable activity bound to two sessions) stays recorded, flagged and quarantined; the session is CONFLICTED for gating and its facts count for neither capacity nor learning until a correction resolves them; a report dated before its activity is rejected.

Without learning consent the athlete model stays empty and no athlete-specific pattern changes the plan; gating on the plan's own completed-work record does not depend on learning consent; the privacy scope of consent stays with Product/Data.
limitations: Pooling assumption is unverified; evidence supports the general approach, not the specific counts and windows.
Self-report quality varies.

recommendations.recommendation: R1 (non-blocking, coaching quality): when a strength step holds only because RIR was not logged, the next session should explicitly ask for reps in reserve on that exercise; a reviewed option is one ADVANCE after two consecutive exposures with target reps met at the planned load and no RIR, never EARNED.

R2 (non-blocking): collect the structured reasonCategory in the product; free text then only adds CLINICAL or ASK. A FAMILY-category reason whose text says a relative was ill currently routes CLINICAL (conservative false positive).
R3 adopted in round 4 (structured category required for a nonclinical break).
R4 adopted in round 5 (nothing/nada as negators).

R5 (non-blocking): ask the athlete to confirm a logged load far below the plan. Probe D: 8 kg logged against 80 kg planned is adopted silently as MODIFY, which is conservative but probably a typo. The numeric threshold is Data-owned.

R6 (non-blocking): treat yes-meaning values in eligibility clinical flags ('true', 1, 'yes', 'sim', 'si') as CLINICAL, as interruptionFacts already does for the interruption flag. Today they ASK, which is safe but inconsistent.

R7 (owned gap, next runtime revision): add birth and baby terms (had a baby, gave birth is already present, bebe, parto), crash and collision terms (crash, collision, hit by, atropelado, atropellado), bites (bitten, mordida) and slips (slipped, escorreguei, resbale) as clinical or ambiguous. Make negated damage statements ('No broken bones', 'Didn't break my leg') ASK instead of CLINICAL.
R8 (non-blocking): when EVENT_AMBITIOUS_FOR_CURRENT_RUNNING applies, collect the athlete's keep-or-change choice before the race window. It stays non-blocking for the preparatory weeks.

R9 (non-blocking): when LONG_RUN_PEAK_BELOW_TARGET is material to the goal, default race-day instructions to completion-focused pacing with optional walk breaks instead of 'decide in the final part whether to press'.

R10 (non-blocking): for athletes whose achieved long run is close to their easy run (restart and walk/jog exits), the taper and next-block fractions make the long run shorter than the easy runs (probe C restart case: taper long 20 with easy 25; next block long 15 with easy 20). Consider bounding the long run below by the easy run, as the share semantics already do.

dossierAnswers.question: Q1 (change 1): event proximity in days, 6-day race window, taper days
dossierAnswers.answer: Yes. Taper evidence is defined in days before competition, so counting days to the race is the right reading of the approved envelope, and the FREEZE-1 calendar-week reading was the defect. A 6-day race window plus 7 taper days per taper week (about two weeks of progressive reduction) sits inside the effective range. The split is operational: it keeps the shakeout on the day before, the touch and the last light strength session at least 3 days out, and the taper long run a week before. Verified on 840 programs over every race weekday. Approved as part of R6-EVENT-TRANSITION, which stays REVISE for D43.

dossierAnswers.question: Q2 (change 2): familiar walk/jog start for non-novices below the minimum session
dossierAnswers.answer: Approved in principle; step 0 is not required. Starting from current running is the cold-start rule, and step 0 would drop a non-novice far below current exposure. As written, though, a session may hold the whole weekly share of running, above the longest current run (56 of 128 raised starts in probe B). Required (D42): start at the highest step whose jogging per session is within both the longest current run and the weekly share. Novices and zero or unknown exposure stay at step 0, which is already correct.

dossierAnswers.question: Q5 (change 5): one increment above the planned load for logged-load adoption
dossierAnswers.answer: One smallest increment is an acceptable size bound for rows that state a planned load, and pound conversion and refusing unknown units are correct. Size is not evidence, though. Required (D44): adopt an above-plan load only when that exposure met the ADVANCE criterion (target reps, minimum logged RIR >= prescribed RIR - 1, no adverse response); otherwise keep the planned load and ask. Establishment rows state no load, so the bound does not apply to them. Required (D45): no unconfirmed single establishment log becomes a numeric prescription. Recommended (R5): confirm logged loads far below the plan.

dossierAnswers.question: Q11 (change 11): widened clinical lexicon and damage-verb plus body-part rule
dossierAnswers.answer: Accepted inside the owned-gap decision of round 6. The additions only add CLINICAL or ASK outcomes, every earlier battery phrase keeps its outcome, and the judge's misses now route CLINICAL or ASK. New residuals (birth, crashes, bites, slips) and the conservative false positive on negated damage are recorded as recommendation R7 for the next runtime revision. They are not blocking, because the structured category and current eligibility remain the primary defence. Structured-path defects would still block; none was found.

dossierAnswers.question: Q13 (change 13): does walk/jog-only preparation before a race need a blocking ASK?
dossierAnswers.answer: No whole-program blocking ASK is required. The preparatory walk/jog weeks are the right training whatever the athlete decides, and withholding them helps no one. The non-blocking negotiation is not enough on its own, however, while race week and race day contradict it: today walk/jog athletes get continuous runs they have not reached, and walk/jog, restart and below-minimum athletes race at race effort with strides. Required (D43): event sessions follow the run mode; race day is a completion with walk breaks at conversational effort, with no strides and no press; warm-up strides only after executed strides; and the negotiation states the gap and offers keep-with-walk-breaks or a later or shorter event. Recommended (R8): collect that choice before the race window.

dossierAnswers.question: Confirmations: changes 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12
dossierAnswers.answer: Confirmed (3) the entry ceiling in every projected week; (4) load units at intake and in logs, with dose history above six sets; (6) sets returning one per executed week; (7) missing gates in reviews, though the projection still needs D46; (8) the append-only record with conflicts quarantined, and one activity on two sessions conflicting on both; (9) the coaching side of consent, the privacy scope staying with Product/Data; (10) interruption facts, yes-meaning flags and the minimum demonstration; (12) an unavailable race date being asked. Recommended (R6): treat yes-meaning eligibility flags as CLINICAL rather than ASK.
